title: ZFP36L2 orchestrates stress-adaptive plasticity in regeneration and cancer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all five GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) subseries folders and downloaded and parsed 8 processed CSVs (<4 MB each). HyperTRIBE (RNA-editing binding assay) site tables: MSK107LI 57,803 sites / 8,401 genes, OKG146LI 111,139 sites / 10,769 genes, both unfiltered (padj up to 1); OKG146N (7,016 rows) and OKG146P (18,947) contain only padj<0.05 sites. Gene-level 3' UTR binding calls agree across lines: 756 of 775 MSK107LI-bound genes are also bound in OKG146LI (7,236 shared genes). Actinomycin D decay tables contain only significant genes (5,152 and 2,833 rows, all padj<0.05); MSK107LI file has 15,317 blank rows; cross-line Spearman of decay_diff = 0.13 on 1,381 shared genes. SLAM-seq (metabolic-labelling half-life) table: 5,888 genes by symbol only, 5,133 with fit R2>0.5 in both arms; some knockdown half-lives are absurd fit failures (up to 4.4e21). Bulk RNA-seq counts: 78,986 genes x 12 samples. The 2.0 GB scRNA-seq h5ad was not downloaded.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That half-lives are in hours (column has no unit; median 5.0 fits hours), the HyperTRIBE design (wild-type versus RNA-binding-dead ZFP36L2 fused to ADAR), the 5 h actinomycin D chase, and the paper's 379-gene shared decay-target count, which I did not reproduce. Supplementary tables were not retrievable from Europe PMC.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked in files: all processed CSVs download openly from the GEO FTP (file transfer) site, no login needed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in files: the binding label is site-level padj/diff_mean in one file, so a per-gene 'bound in the 3' UTR' call is a groupby inside one table, not inference across sources. The stabilisation label is log2 of two half-life columns in the same table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked in files: no sequences are included. Inputs come from one bulk GENCODE/Ensembl 3' UTR FASTA joined on ENSG IDs, which is one download, not thousands of lookups. The SLAM-seq table has gene symbols only, so it needs symbol-to-ID mapping.

a4_units_stated.note: Checked in files: editing fractions are proportions from 0 to 1. Half-life columns carry no unit; the paper implies hours and the median of 5.0 is consistent with that. Marginal pass.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked in files: 10,769 genes with HyperTRIBE calls in OKG146LI (6,067 significant), 7,236 genes shared with MSK107LI, and 5,133 well-fitted SLAM-seq half-life pairs.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~10 MB of CSVs plus ~50 MB of 3' UTR FASTA
a6_fits_laptop.note: Tabular data and sequence embeddings fit easily on a CPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Partly checked: the GEO subseries match the data statement. Exact gene counts were not compared because the paper's supplementary tables could not be retrieved, but nothing contradicts the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are wet-lab measurements: ADAR editing frequencies and 4sU (4-thiouridine) labelling half-lives, not model outputs. One caveat: whether an edit is detected depends on how highly the gene is expressed, so expression is a confounder, though not circular.

B1.why: Several per-line CSVs join on ENSG; SLAM-seq table joins only by gene symbol (seen in files).

B2.why: Parse fine but need fixes: trailing empty column, 15,317 blank rows, half-lives up to 4.4e21 (seen).

B3.why: Same lab and assay, but four organoid lines have different depth; per-line normalisation needed (seen).

B4.why: No censoring, but failed half-life fits (~13% with R2<0.5) must be dropped (seen in files).

B5.why: No duplicate genes in decay or SLAM-seq tables; HyperTRIBE is one row per edit site (seen).

B6.why: No README; column names are mostly self-explanatory, but half-life units and test direction are undocumented (seen).

C1.why: Whether sequence models add anything beyond counting AU-rich motifs is informative, but the result could just be 'motif count suffices'.

C2.why: No ZFP36L2-specific predictor found; general RBP (RNA-binding protein) and half-life models exist but weren't trained on this. Likely novel.

C3.why: Novel: HyperTRIBE and SLAM-seq on human colorectal cancer organoids, published August 2026, never modelled.

C4.why: HyperTRIBE needs cloning, transduction and sequencing per cell type; a predictor would only partly replace it.

C5.why: Obvious dummy baselines: UAUUUAU 7-mer count, AREScore (AU-rich element score), 3' UTR length, expression level.

D1.why: RNA-FM and Orthrus (RNA/mRNA language models) have downloadable open weights.

D2.why: Embed ~11k 3' UTRs once on CPU, then fit logistic or ridge head; chunk long UTRs.

D3.why: Licences not checked for this evaluation; assume research use is acceptable.

E1.why: Hold out 3' UTR sequence-similarity clusters or whole chromosomes; edit-site coordinates are in event_id.

E2.why: Thousands of genes; 22+ chromosomes or many clusters available as groups.

E3.why: Majority class, 7-mer count and expression-only logistic baselines computable from the files.

E4.why: Two lines give a replicate ceiling: 756/775 bound-gene agreement, versus decay Spearman 0.13 (computed).

E5.why: UAUUUAU / AUUUA motif enrichment in bound 3' UTRs is the known ZFP36 family signal.

E6.why: Label shuffling, and fitting on expression or UTR length alone, are runnable.

E7.why: Mouse ZFP36L2 target sets (NAR 2022, RNA Biology 2026) and ZFP36 PAR-CLIP give outside validation.

E8.why: Paper reports overlaps and enrichments, not a predictive metric to reproduce.

G1.why: Ensembl gene IDs and hg38 coordinates of edit sites present in files.

G2.why: GENCODE 3' UTR sequences and the Saluki half-life compendium (39 human datasets) join on Ensembl gene.

G3.why: Gene-to-many 3' UTR isoforms; need a collapse rule, e.g. longest or most-expressed transcript.

G4.why: Linking binding to half-life across cell types is somewhat bigger, but only one cancer type is measured here.

H1.why: HyperTRIBE in two lines includes non-significant sites; decay tables keep only significant genes.

H2.why: Four organoid lines from two colorectal cancer patients; one tissue, one lab.

H3.why: Claim is precise: predicts ZFP36L2 3' UTR binding in expressed genes of colorectal cancer organoids.

H4.why: Paper says organoid-specific, but the filtering of the decay tables is visible only in the files.

I1.why: RNA-binding protein and mRNA decay researchers; no specific named user group.

I2.why: Could prioritise candidate targets for validation, but only marginally over motif scanning.

I3.why: PR-AUC (precision-recall area under the curve) roughly matches 'which genes to validate'.

I4.why: Motif counting may capture most signal; tissue specificity suggests context adds something.

J1.why: Embeddings, grouped splits, confounder control, cross-species transfer.

J2.why: AU-rich biology is intuitive, but separating expression bias needs care.

J3.why: A cleaned gene-level binding and half-life table plus a motif baseline is shareable alone.

J4.why: Roughly two weekends; not formally fixed.

J5.why: Kill condition proposed below but not yet written in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: AREScore (rule-based AU-rich element score, used in prior ZFP36L2 papers)
existing_models.score_and_split: Heuristic with no trained split; scores pentamer count, spacing and AU context.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The 2026 RNA Biology mouse study says ZFP36L2 targeting is tissue-specific and depends on more than AU-rich elements.

existing_models.name: RBPNet / iDeepB (deep models of RBP binding at single-base resolution, trained on eCLIP (enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation) data)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported on eCLIP data for many RBPs; I did not confirm that ZFP36L2 is among them, and saw no split details.

existing_models.name: Saluki (Agarwal & Kelley 2022, Genome Biology; mRNA half-life from sequence)
existing_models.score_and_split: r=0.77 for half-life across a compendium of 39 human datasets; not ZFP36L2-dependent change.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or Orthrus (RNA/mRNA language models) on 3' UTR sequences
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU; ~11k UTRs chunked to 1 kb
backbone.licence: Not verified; assumed open for research use

integration.partner_dataset: GENCODE 3' UTR sequences plus the Saluki half-life compendium and mouse ZFP36L2 target sets
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene ID (and hg38 coordinates for edit sites)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does 3' UTR sequence context beyond the AU-rich motif determine which transcripts ZFP36L2 binds and destabilises, and does this transfer between human cancer organoids and mouse tissues?

controls.positive_control: UAUUUAU 7-mer count must separate bound from unbound 3' UTRs (AUC well above 0.5); predicting 3' UTR length from embeddings should be near-perfect.
controls.negative_control: Shuffled labels collapse to majority class; a model on expression level alone sets the confounder floor.
controls.external_validation: Mouse ZFP36L2 targets (NAR 2022 and RNA Biology 2026 papers) and the ZFP36 PAR-CLIP targets in HEK293 cells (Genome Biology 2014).

honest_claim_h3: Predicts which expressed genes ZFP36L2 binds in their 3' UTR in two human colorectal cancer liver-metastasis organoid lines, among genes deep enough to detect editing.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the RNA sequence after a gene's coding region to predict whether the cancer-mutated protein ZFP36L2 binds it and speeds its decay.
plain_idea.train_on: The 3' untranslated region sequence of each gene, plus its expression level, for 10,769 genes measured in one organoid line (7,236 measured in two lines).
plain_idea.predict: Whether ZFP36L2 binds the gene, as measured by HyperTRIBE (a fused RNA-editing enzyme marks bound RNAs), and secondarily how much the gene's half-life changes when ZFP36L2 is knocked down (SLAM-seq).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Researchers studying ZFP36L2 in cancer and regeneration could rank candidate targets in new cell types without running an editing experiment, and we'd learn whether simple motif counting already explains binding.

more_or_better_data.why: This is the first human-organoid ZFP36L2 binding set with negatives (~10.8k genes); general RBP models use eCLIP from K562/HepG2 cell lines, and I didn't confirm they include ZFP36L2.

confidence_score.why: Two independent lines give per-gene agreement (756/775 concordant), usable to flag uncertain genes; AREScore gives no confidence.

models_beatable.why: The closest baseline is a hand-crafted motif score (AREScore); Saluki (2022) predicts absolute half-life rather than ZFP36L2-dependent change.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing ZFP36L2-specific model sees a subset of our inputs on the same split, so improvement isn't guaranteed by construction.

label_elsewhere.sources: Mouse ZFP36L2 target sets (NAR 2022; RNA Biology 2026, found by search); ZFP36 PAR-CLIP targets (Genome Biology 2014, found by search); POSTAR3 CLIP database (known resource, ZFP36L2 coverage unverified).
label_elsewhere.join_key: Ensembl gene ID / gene symbol (mouse via orthologs)
label_elsewhere.why: Small outside target sets allow an external transfer test, but give little extra training data.

risks: Paralogous genes with similar 3' UTRs placed in both train and test.
Detecting editing depends on read depth, so highly expressed genes look 'bound'; the model may learn expression, not binding.
Long 3' UTRs have more chances to be edited, so length alone may predict the label.
The decay and OKG146N/P files contain only significant genes, so using them as labels removes the negatives.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole chromosomes (from event_id coordinates, seen in files), or cluster 3' UTRs at ~80% identity with MMseqs2 and hold out clusters; train on OKG146LI and test on MSK107LI as a second axis.
checks: Shuffle labels and confirm collapse to the majority-class baseline.
Fit expression-only and UTR-length-only models; the sequence model must beat both, and be evaluated within expression-matched bins.
Nearest-neighbour UTR identity between test and train genes.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: duplicates are easy to handle, but expression and length confounding is a serious risk that needs explicit stratification.

success_criteria.metric: PR-AUC (precision-recall area under the curve) for 3' UTR binding on held-out chromosomes within expression-matched bins, because the use is picking genes to validate.
success_criteria.baselines: Majority class (prevalence ~0.56 of genes in OKG146LI, computed: 6,067 of 10,769 significant at any site); UAUUUAU 7-mer count, AREScore and expression-only logistic regression (to be computed; no published number exists).
success_criteria.success: PR-AUC at least 0.05 above the best of the motif-count and expression baselines on held-out chromosomes, and transfer to MSK107LI calls; no published target number exists.
success_criteria.noise_ceiling: Cross-line agreement: 756 of 775 MSK107LI-bound genes also bound in OKG146LI; 2,516 bound only in OKG146LI (mostly depth-driven).
success_criteria.kill: Embedding model under 0.03 PR-AUC better than 7-mer count plus expression after one weekend.

ambitious.why: Publishes RBP target-specificity work (including the 2022 ZFP36L2 paper); needs sequence context beyond the motif that transfers to mouse.

realistic.why: Takes focused analyses of RBP targeting rules; fits a 'motif plus context' result on one dataset.

fallback.journal: bioRxiv preprint / NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics
fallback.why: A negative result ('motif count explains binding') with a cleaned table is publishable as a short note.

pitch.headline: Organoid-measured ZFP36L2 binding for 10,769 genes, with 756 of 775 bound genes reproduced in a second line, never used for ML.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Unfiltered HyperTRIBE site tables (padj up to 1, so negatives included) from human colorectal cancer metastasis organoids, paired with SLAM-seq half-lives for 5,133 well-fitted genes with and without knockdown.
pitch.the_win: A sequence model beating UAUUUAU motif count plus expression by at least 0.05 PR-AUC on held-out chromosomes and transferring to mouse target sets.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A clean statement that ZFP36L2 binding in these organoids is explained by AU-rich motif count and expression, plus a deduplicated gene-level table.
pitch.who_wants_it: Groups studying ZFP36 family RNA decay in cancer and immunity, deciding which predicted targets to validate.

ml_idea: Gene-level classifier: GENCODE 3' UTR sequence (frozen RNA-FM/Orthrus embeddings, plus k-mer counts) and expression predict ZFP36L2 HyperTRIBE binding in OKG146LI; test on held-out chromosomes, transfer to MSK107LI and mouse target sets; secondary regression on log2 SLAM-seq half-life ratio.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: ~11k UTRs chunked to 1 kb at ~2 chunks/s on CPU for embeddings; logistic regression CV is seconds.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Compute PR-AUC of UAUUUAU count plus log expression for OKG146LI gene-level binding; if it is already near the cross-line ceiling, stop.

verdict_reason: Open, small and never-modelled binding and half-life tables pass Part A, but model-readiness is 7/12 (filtered decay tables, failed fits, no README). The dataset covers one tissue from two patients, and expression and motif-count confounding may leave nothing for a sequence model to add.
